intervals.label: collaboration (GENIUS proposal to end of GENIUS-TF)
intervals.note: Lower bound: the 1997 proposal of the GENIUS project; the collaboration's founding date is not published. End: the end of the GENIUS-TF run (2003-2006, thesis).
intervals.quote: The goal of GENIUS-TF was to test some key operational parameters of the full GENIUS project proposal in 1997

intervals.label: completed (GENIUS-TF ended)
intervals.note: No source states that the collaboration was dissolved; this follows the end of its only built set-up, GENIUS-TF.
intervals.quote: the Genius-TF setup has run a total of six HPGe detectors during three years (2003–2006)

name: GENIUS Collaboration
notes: No roster or member count was found; the Atlas records no memberships. The full GENIUS project (a large tank of bare Ge detectors for dark matter, double-beta decay and solar neutrinos, proposed 1997) is not recorded as an experiment: no source read names a host site and approval for it.

summary.plain: The Heidelberg-led group behind GENIUS, a proposal to put bare germanium crystals directly in liquid nitrogen to cut radioactive background, and behind its small Gran Sasso test version GENIUS-TF.
summary.technical: Group of the Max-Planck-Institut fuer Kernphysik, Heidelberg (spokesman: H.V. Klapdor-Kleingrothaus, 'Spokesman of HEIDELBERG-MOSCOW and GENIUS Collaborations'). GENIUS proposed in 1997; GENIUS-TF built and run at LNGS 2003-2006.
